newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares hit new highs, more gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares hit new highs, more gains expected.

text.p: Danish share prices closed at all-time highs on Tuesday, with dealers seeing the prospect of fresh records on Wednesday.

The KFX top-20 index gained 0.55 point to 122.27 and the all-share index rose 0.58 point to 428.95, in overall bourse turnover of 1.03 billion crowns. The previous closing highs were 121.74 and 428.37, respectively.
"We certainly have a volatile market at the moment but I expected us to go further up again tomorrow," a dealer said.
The KFX September future rose 0.60 point to 122.20, with 521 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Among the prime movers were SAS Denmark, which rose three crowns -- 4.8 percent -- to 66 crowns in turnover of 180,000 shares traded in what was seen as a slight over-correction after several days of falls on fears of a price war with new rivals.

A.P. Moeller's two constituent shares -- DS Svendborg B and DS 1912 B -- rose 1,000 crowns each, to 202,000 and 141,000 crowns respectively expectations of increased middle east production by the group's oil units.
Novo Nordisk rose 12 crowns to 901, in a move that dealers were unable to explain. --Uffe Hansen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969658
